races.name: Queen Anne Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Cicero's Gift
runners_data.note: Charles Hills runner with solid form at this trip on Good ground including a recent win, but this seven-horse glut of prominent types means Jason Watson is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal, which historically does not draw the best from this horse.
runners_data.comment: Cicero's Gift has won twice in its last five starts and acts on soft, good and AW, but the ground here may be on the quick side for this one, and last time out's seventh in the Lockinge — beaten over seven lengths — tempers enthusiasm despite that Group 1 backdrop.

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden four-year-old with impressive winning form at nine furlongs, but this is his first crack at a flat mile on fast ground and he has been pushed rearward against his natural grain — James Doyle will need the pace to truly collapse to get him into the race.
runners_data.comment: Damysus arrives on the back of a 6¼-length thumping in a Group 1 at Newbury last time, with lack of pace exposed over a mile, and today's test looks similarly sharp for a horse who really comes into his own at nine or ten furlongs.

runners_data.name: Docklands
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's Mark Zahra-ridden six-year-old ran a fine third at Ascot last time and handles Good ground well; races with headgear and is a genuine front-end horse by nature, yet the strength of this prominent contingent means he is likely to be tracking rather than leading, which slightly softens his profile.
runners_data.comment: Docklands won this race last year and shaped with promise on return when a close third in a Group 1 at Sha Tin 51 days ago, so course-and-distance form reads well; first-time headgear and a trainer in form add appeal, though a rating of 118 versus our figure of 114 suggests the handicapper holds a slight edge.

runners_data.name: First Conquest
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Charlie Appleby on a horse who has been consistently placed at nine and ten furlongs on Good ground, but the drop to a mile, the 179-day absence, and being shuffled out of his preferred prominent position are three compounding concerns that make this a watching brief.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and absent for 179 days, First Conquest shaped respectably with a close third in a Meydan Group 2 last time but looks likely to fill a pacemaking role for better-fancied stablemates here, making it very hard to fancy at big odds.

runners_data.name: More Thunder
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old is lightly weighted in terms of OR but carries full 9st, has won four of his last eight on Good ground, and Tom Marquand is likely to slot him just behind the leader in a position that suits — if Opera Ballo softens the pace, More Thunder's tactical speed is a genuine asset.
runners_data.comment: Ran a career-best when runner-up in the Lockinge Group 1 last time, showing real progression at a mile on a sound surface, and this stiff track could bring him even closer to the principals — though there's a nagging question over whether that ceiling has now been reached.

runners_data.name: Notable Speech
runners_data.note: The William Buick-Charlie Appleby combination carries considerable weight in Group 1 company; three wins at eight furlongs on fast ground and a 2000 Guineas pedigree make him the most credible threat to Opera Ballo, though his last run produced a disappointing fourth and he will need to bounce back sharply.
runners_data.comment: Notable Speech has won five G1s and was imperious when scooting clear in the Lockinge last time, marking it out as probably the world's number-one miler; carrying 128 lb from stall 1, the course record is a minor query but fast ground suits and this is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Opera Ballo
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the race, with five wins from nine on Good surfaces including back-to-back wins at nine furlongs; Billy Loughnane can dictate terms completely unopposed on this straight track, and the headgear flag (h) suggests he is a horse who needs to be ridden positively to show his best.
runners_data.comment: Four wins in its last five starts, Opera Ballo has progressed into one of Europe's leading milers — most recently dictating and winning the bet365 Mile (Group 2) at Sandown by 3l from a multiple G1 winner — and acts on today's conditions. First-time headgear is the one unknown.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old won over seven furlongs on Soft last time but his Good-ground figures are patchy (2W from 15 attempts) and Kieran Shoemark faces the task of finding cover from a prominent horse who will be racing mid-pack against his instincts — the short ten-day turnaround is also a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Ten Bob Tony won a Group 3 at Epsom ten days ago, but that victory came on ground with cut and this looks a stiffer test — rated 108 on our figures and ranked last of nine, there are serious doubts about whether it can match those elite rivals here.

runners_data.name: Zeus Olympios
runners_data.note: KR Burke's four-year-old has an excellent strike rate at eight furlongs on Good ground (3 wins from 5 similar-going runs) and Clifford Lee should find a clean passage mid-race; his recent third-placed efforts on better ground suggest he may be hitting a ceiling at this level, but he is consistent and well-placed tactically.
runners_data.comment: Zeus Olympios arrives on the back of a career-best effort when finishing third in the Lockinge Stakes, and his three wins in his last five starts underline a horse in fine fettle — the main reservation is whether he can quite bridge the gap to outright Group 1 winning class today.

races.paceDynamic: Opera Ballo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner Group 1 mile, and with no natural rival to press him from the gates, Billy Loughnane can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground. More Thunder and Notable Speech are genuine prominent types who will sit in behind, likely tracking Opera Ballo through the straight-mile layout at Ascot where the lack of a bend means pace tends to be measured and the leader rarely faces a genuine sprint test until late. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all secure their natural positions — Cicero's Gift, Docklands, First Conquest and Ten Bob Tony are true prominent racers who are likely to be squeezed into a midfield role against their instincts, which blunts their chance. This race shape strongly favours horses who can either control from the front and quicken on a flat, true surface, or those with the class and tactical awareness to track the pace closely in second or third and produce a sharp finishing effort — pure hold-up horses face the most disadvantage given the lack of a truly strong gallop.

watchPoints.text: Opera Ballo's ability to dictate completely unchallenged is the central tactical question — if he goes out at a crawl, the field will bunch dangerously in the final two furlongs with no natural hold-up horse to benefit.

Notable Speech produced a flat fourth last time out, and if that run reflects a dip in form rather than a tactical blip, the Appleby stable's main hope may underperform at a short price — watch the market for any support signal.

Docklands and Cicero's Gift both want to race prominently but physically cannot both be in the front two — one or both will be shuffled back early and may lose competitive rhythm in the process, creating a pocket of disruption behind Opera Ballo.

The ground is Good to Firm across the entire card, identical for all races — no runner has a meaningful going concern flagged, but horses who have winning form specifically on Fast or Firm ground (Notable Speech: 3 wins on Firm) may receive an added subtle edge over those who are purely Good-ground performers.

First Conquest returns after 179 days off for Charlie Appleby; Ryan Moore's booking suggests connections are bullish, but the long absence combined with a trip shorter than any of his recent runs makes it worth monitoring how freely he travels in the early stages as a guide to whether the layoff has left him short.

races.name: Coventry Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay Of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Three wins from three starts over 5f on Good, now stepping up to 6f which remains a question, and Hugo Palmer's filly carries strong form but her natural prominent style cannot be accommodated in a field this deep with pace — she will be pushed into a midfield berth she does not naturally occupy.
runners_data.comment: Rattled off back-to-back wins before a game half-length second in Listed company latest, and acts on today's going and distance, making this high-class colt a genuine threat — the main concern is whether he's now near his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Bull Shark
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over and the horse has shown consistency with four places from four runs, but an unclassified style, a drop from 7f and a record of four consecutive runner-up or third-place finishes over 5-7f does not inspire confidence that he has the gears to win a Group 2 on Good to Firm ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but not without appeal — Bull Shark quickened clear latest at The Curragh only to be caught late, suggesting timing rather than ability was the issue. A very useful sprint prospect who acts on varying ground, though ranked 18th on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's colt has only one run to his name — a second over this exact course and distance on Good — and while that is a solid reference point, the stable has had no winners in the last 14 days and Cilician's genuine front-running style will be difficult to express in a field this packed with pace.
runners_data.comment: Cilician shaped with distinct promise on debut, going down by just half a length at Nottingham over today's trip, and speed in the pedigree suggests the six furlongs suits; however, winless in recent starts and carrying 129lb from stall 9, there's still plenty to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount for the Ballydoyle operation and Confucius won his debut at 6f on Good before placing at 5f on Heavy; his natural prominent style is sound for this trip but the sheer number of similar types means he will not get his ideal position, and Moore's race-craft becomes his biggest asset.
runners_data.comment: Confucius took a Naas maiden by four lengths last time, that form already looking solid, and he gets the nod from the top course jockey in a yard that won this 12 months ago; open to further progress and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Cut A Dash
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's debutant winner over 5f Good for Sean Levey — a single run makes assessment difficult and he has never faced 6f, so the extra furlong is an unknown; his prominent style is genuine but he, like several others, will be funnelled into a midfield berth he cannot avoid given the field's composition.
runners_data.comment: Won on debut at York with plenty in hand, quickening clear cosily by three lengths on good ground over today's trip, and that novice form looks strong enough to merit this step up in class — the sole risk is how she handles 34 days off and the rise in grade.

runners_data.name: Easy Answer
runners_data.note: Michael Bell sends out this colt with one run — a third over this exact 6f course on Good — and Cristian Demuro is a capable booking, but the unclassified style and single race outing make him one of the harder horses to assess with confidence; lightly raced flag applies.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of promise on debut at Yarmouth, finishing third — best of those held up — beaten just 1¼ lengths, and should improve stepping forward from that initial experience if ridden more positively over today's trip, though winless in recent starts remains the caveat.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: A second over 6f Good on debut for the Al Jehani yard with Bughenaim aboard; mapped to hold-up due to redistribution from midfield rather than true nature, so any closing run should be read with that caveat firmly in mind — this is not a confirmed hold-up horse.
runners_data.comment: Promising debut second at Lingfield, beaten 3l while finishing well after being outpaced, suggests ability — first-time headgear adds interest — but stepping up in class leaves Final Objective looking vulnerable despite that speed pedigree over today's trip.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: William Buick partners this James Ferguson-trained debut winner over 6f Good, and the 32-day break is manageable; his true style is prominent racing and he would ideally be pressing the pace, but the field density means he must accept a midfield slot, which Buick has the skill to turn to advantage if the pace genuinely tests the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Scored on debut at Newbury, quickening well to win by 1¼l, but that maiden form reads nothing special and our figures rank it well below most here — further progress needed to compete at this level.

runners_data.name: Great Barrier Reef
runners_data.note: Two wins from two starts over 6f, including on soft ground, for the Aidan O'Brien first-string team with Wayne Lordan, and he is one of the prominent types most likely to actually secure a position close to The Scallionator given his course experience — the standout profile for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins culminate in a Curragh Group 3 success last time, where he had a bit in hand and looked like 7f is well within compass — stiff track, sound surface and proven distance all in his favour, with the yard having won this last year. The main risk is handling a large field from stall 3.

runners_data.name: High King
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's charge won well over 6f Good last time after a distant debut, and Gavin Ryan keeps the ride; a genuine prominent racer with a solid 6f record who should be competitive for a handy early position, though the field depth means even he may face early jostling.
runners_data.comment: Franked a taking Fairyhouse win with an excellent turn of foot, and that 3½-length success reads well stepping up in class; the unplaced run on the other side of that coin and a stiff 129lb are the checks on enthusiasm here.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's filly has three placings from three starts over 5f Good for Rossa Ryan; she steps up from 5f to 6f here which is a genuine unknown, and her redistribution to hold-up from natural midfield means a late flourish is less certain than her map position implies.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless in recent starts, Jaan Ki Tukri has placed in all three latest outings and acts on today's going and distance — though stepping up in class looks the key test from stall 22 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Kamaal
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners this Jack Jones-trained colt who ran fifth on his sole start over 6f Good — the lightly-raced flag is fully warranted and an unclassified style adds further opacity; it is difficult to build a strong case from one moderate run in a Group 2.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and beaten three lengths on a modest Newbury maiden debut 32 days ago, Kamaal looks out of depth stepping up in class here, though today's trip and going hold no fears — a big ask at the foot of the weights.

runners_data.name: Mrair
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for George Scott and Mrair has won and placed over this exact 6f Good combination; two runs, both over course and distance, give him the clearest profile match for the dominant scenario, and Murphy is ideally suited to tracking the pace and striking late in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Won a Lingfield novice by 3l on latest but that came in weaker company, and greenness remains a concern under 129lb from stall 14; with a trainer in form and more improvement likely as experience grows, the upside is real if inexperience doesn't cost.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's two-from-two filly has won over 6f on both soft and Good, and Charles Bishop keeps the ride after 25 days off; a genuine prominent racer with proper 6f form who is one of the realistic contenders for a position just off the early lead — course and distance form is a key plus.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, including a smooth Goodwood success last time, give Night In Vegas solid claims, and the step up in class looks the obvious next test; acts on good and effective at today's trip, though 129 lb from stall 21 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Royal Heritage
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this Al Jehani runner who won on soft ground six days ago, making this a very quick turnaround; the 6f debut win on soft leaves a going question for Good to Firm, and the short rest after a first career run adds an additional risk factor despite the promising form line.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a comfortable 3-length debut win at Hamilton six days ago and acts on good to soft over this trip, but the quick turnaround and a provisional rating of 102 ranked 15th of 22 suggest there are open questions — an improver worth noting, albeit untested beyond that promising maiden.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Pride
runners_data.note: James McDonald partners K R Burke's debutant winner over 5f Good, stepping up 1f in trip for the first time; redistributed to hold-up from natural midfield, so his map position does not reflect a true closing style — McDonald will seek a prominent enough berth to let the horse's speed tell.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up on debut at Ayr and that form has been franked, marking this one out as potentially very useful stepping up in class; acts on the going and trip, though the hefty 129lb and draw 17 are factors to weigh against a short sample of evidence.

runners_data.name: Siouxperb
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's debut winner over 6f Good for Hector Crouch returns after 56 days — the longest break of any runner here — and that absence after a single run introduces a fitness question that cannot be overlooked, even with a promising performance on the clock.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by four lengths on debut at Yarmouth, quickening clear with plenty in hand, and stays today's trip on this ground — a smart prospect returning off a short break, though 129 lb and 56 days off give rivals something to aim at.

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's colt won well over 6f Good last time out for Kieran Shoemark after a distant debut over the same course; two runs both at 6f on Good is the ideal form profile for this race and Shoemark's hold of the ride suggests strong stable confidence.
runners_data.comment: Followed up debut experience with a narrow novice win at Nottingham 13 days ago, but this represents a sharp step up in grade and, ranked 16th of 22 on our figures, considerably more improvement will be needed to make an impact here.

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this M D O'Callaghan runner who won on soft ground nine days ago — another very quick reappearance — and the ability to win on soft is noted, though Good to Firm is a notably different surface test; Keane's front-rank riding style suits the prominent profile here.
runners_data.comment: Scraped home by a nose on debut at Goodwood nine days ago, with the form nothing special and the win flattered by a pace collapse — hard to fancy at the foot of the weights on these figures, though the scope to progress with that run under its belt offers the only realistic hook.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce's mount is the only confirmed front-runner in the field and holds the key tactical card; a winner over 6f Good last time from an outside draw, his ability to control the tempo is the defining feature of this race shape, though his style-fit tag suggests he may be vulnerable if the pace proves too extreme for him.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Listowel maiden by three lengths 16 days ago and is clearly progressing, though carrying 129lb from stall 16 is a notable ask stepping into stronger company; breeding points to 6f/7f on good ground as the sweet spot, so conditions at least play to strengths.

runners_data.name: Treasurer
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' debutant ran fourth over 6f Good 16 days ago with Rowan Scott aboard; a fourth on debut with an unclassified style is the thinnest profile in the race and the lightly-raced flag underlines how much improvement is needed to be competitive at Group 2 level.
runners_data.comment: Promising 3l fourth on debut at Nottingham shows ability, and today's trip and conditions suit, but ranked 19th of 22 on our figures, Treasurer has plenty to find in this company despite likely improvement still to come.

runners_data.name: Arizona Raider
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's second string to The Scallionator, ridden by W J Lee; won over 1m Good most recently in a clear step up in trip profile and is a natural prominent racer who will be displaced into midfield — the 1m win is an unusual prep for a 6f Group 2 sprint and raises the question of whether his best form is actually at shorter.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Roscommon auction race last time on the step up in trip and drop in class, but ranks near the foot of the weights here and looks vulnerable at this level, with sounder ground at least suiting his action.

races.paceDynamic: The Scallionator is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field and, crucially, is unlikely to face serious early pressure from a rival pacesetter — Wesley Joyce will be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front rather than being dragged into a true test of stamina. Behind him, the race shape is heavily congested: Great Barrier Reef, High King, Mrair, Night In Vegas, The Ginger Kid, Siouxperb, The Harv, Royal Heritage and Cilician are all natural prominent-racing types competing for the same ground just off the leader, meaning several will inevitably be pushed wider or further back than they want. This field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — the horses most likely to actually secure a position close to The Scallionator are Great Barrier Reef (two wins over course-and-distance trips, strong Aidan O'Brien team), Mrair (Oisin Murphy, two 6f wins), and Night In Vegas (consistent 6f winner with strong Ascot form), while God Given Talent, Confucius, Cut A Dash, Adaay Of Scarlett and Arizona Raider — all natural prominent racers — are mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for them. The resulting race shape strongly favours horses who travel comfortably in the first three to five lengths of the leader and can produce a sustained gallop from two furlongs out, rather than late closers who will face traffic on a track where position and early momentum are paramount at 6f on Good to Firm ground.

races.name: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for Kevin Ryan who has been placed in similar-going before (sim-going 11/15) but recent form reads 007-09 and she is likely to be finishing late into a wall of traffic in a 26-runner sprint.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and again disappointing at York last time, Ain't Nobody is very erratic and not always resolute, though first-time headgear may sharpen focus, and it does hold course-and-distance form on today's ground.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has won three of his last seven on similar going and on 5f, and Paul Mulrennan can get him close to the pace where his form figures read best; the soft-ground wins are numerous but the Good to Firm record is encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Won this race last year and arrives in decent nick after finishing second in a Group 2 on latest start, so course-and-distance form stacks up well; the 133 lb burden from stall 18 is the obvious query, though a progressive return to form suggests fitness is no concern.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: The sole genuine front-runner in this field; Michael Appleby's four-year-old will lead from stall to furlong marker unchallenged, and the absence of a pace rival is a structural advantage rarely available in a 26-runner Group 1 sprint, though his last few runs have been on Good or softer.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 last time out, that run probably needed after 34 days off, Big Mojo is well-suited by today's 6f on fast ground and holds strong claims off 117 — the risk is getting caught too far back again as last year here showed.

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: James McDonald takes over on Simon and Ed Crisford's six-year-old who has four wins on 5f on similar ground and is well placed to race prominently; 80 days off the track is the main question mark, though the trainer has a strong 14-day record.|
runners_data.comment: Held every chance on form credentials — acts on any going over 5f — but well held in a Group 1 last time and ranks 22nd of 26 on our figures; the first-time headgear and 80-day break add further uncertainty for a horse that simply may not be up to this level.

runners_data.name: Getreadytorumble
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's four-year-old is a front-runner by nature with five recent runs between 5f soft and good, but in this congested field the pace positions are genuinely unavailable for all who want them, so Callum Rodriguez may find himself further back than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 last time — fair enough form — and Listed-placed with good prior profile, but ranked 21 of 26 on our figures and needs more improvement again to trouble these; the wide draw in a large field adds no help.

runners_data.name: Jakajaro
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's five-year-old has won twice at 5f on Good and carries solid form into this, but with Cowell having no runners in the last 14 days of note and the horse a natural early-mover, he is one of several genuine pace types who will find the front portion of this field already claimed.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped well when fourth in a Group 2 last time, going down by just 1¼ lengths only near the finish, and two wins in its last five starts show the progressive profile — yet stepping into this grade still leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for the Quinn yard who won at 5f on Soft last time; he wants to be involved from the start but the mathematics of a 26-runner sprint mean Jason Hart faces an early battle just to reach his preferred slot.|
runners_data.comment: Shock Group 2 winner last year, but JM Jungle has failed to recapture that form this season, beaten seven lengths in a Group 2 last time — hard to fancy at these weights from stall 14, even if the trip and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Night Raider
runners_data.note: K R Burke's five-year-old has back-to-back wins at 5f on Soft and Good, James Doyle rides, and the trainer's 14-day record of 8/39 is active; this horse is one of the few genuine prominent types where the position looks genuinely achievable, and recent form is sharply upward.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins culminate in a career-best Temple Stakes Group 2 success at Haydock last time out, and with conditions and trip squarely in favour, Night Raider arrives in fine trim just 24 days later — the main risk is whether the bold front-running style holds up at this level.

runners_data.name: Overpass
runners_data.note: Australian seven-year-old trained by Bjorn Baker, 73 days since his last run and Joshua Parr makes the trip; best form has come at 6f-7f on Good and the drop to 5f looks a concern, regardless of his prominent racing style.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent G1 performer whose T J Smith Stakes fourth (beaten 2l) sets the standard here, and dropping in trip to a stiff track plays to his strengths; yet to win in recent starts but rates clear top on our figures and will be tough to peg back.

runners_data.name: Rumstar
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's six-year-old ran second at 5f on Good last time, 45 days ago; Rob Hornby gets the ride and the horse is a prominent racer whose sim-going record reads well, though the trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a close second in a Group 3 on fast ground latest, and suits today's trip and conditions well; yet to score in recent starts and faces a stiff ask at this level after being outclassed here last year, but is clearly in better shape now.

runners_data.name: Shagraan
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's five-year-old has three wins at 5f including on Soft and Good, and Hector Crouch takes the ride; a front-running inclination means this horse ideally wants to be bowling along in the top five, but the available prominent positions look filled before he arrives.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite last time in the Temple Stakes but holds Listed-class form over this trip and going — a multiple winner at this level who retains claims stepping back from Group company, though that Haydock flop leaves a question mark hanging over current form.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's five-year-old was last seen finishing sixth at 5f on Good just 17 days ago, and Rossa Ryan rides; the sim-going record of 9/15 with zero wins at 5f on this ground profile is a concern, and the horse has struggled to translate a prominent style into results on Good recently.|
runners_data.comment: Showed Group 1 class and ran encouragingly in this race last year, but winless in recent starts and must prove that sharpness is back after a stud sabbatical; the Carlisle Listed run 17 days ago should strip fitness forward.

runners_data.name: Asfoora
runners_data.note: Henry Dwyer's seven-year-old mare won at 5f on Soft last time and Oisin Murphy takes over; carries tongue-tie and breast-girth, and the two blank runs on Good going (10th and 12th) in her last five are a flag given today's Good to Firm conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Defends her 2024 crown here, but two unplaced efforts this term — including a poor showing on easy ground at Haydock last time — raise questions about current form; the tongue-tie is new, fast ground suits, and a bounce-back from this proven G1 winner can't be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's six-year-old mare has two wins at 5f including on Standard and Good ground, Daniel Tudhope rides, and she carries tongue-tie and breast-girth; she races prominently but with so many pace types in this field, her mapped midfield position reflects the grid reality rather than her preferred running order.|
runners_data.comment: Azure Angel steps up sharply in class after a creditable Listed effort last time, but at 130 lb from stall 25 and ranked 24 of 26 on our figures, the step into this grade looks a tough ask — first-time blinkers are a plus, though.

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old has two wins at 5f including on Soft, and Cieren Fallon partners her; 45 days since last run and a recent ninth on Good ground last time are negatives, and she is a pace-style runner who will find herself swept further back than ideal in this traffic.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a G3 success in recent starts but has disappointed twice since, including a 6½-length beating last time out 45 days ago; acts on today's going and distance, yet improvement is needed if that winning form is to resurface.

runners_data.name: Frost At Dawn
runners_data.note: William Buick's mount for William Knight has a 10/15 sim-going record but wins only on Good to Soft or Soft; the headgear (visor) is retained and while the prominent style suits the race shape in theory, his position in the field will be determined by the crowd ahead of him.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and below-par at Haydock last time on easy ground, Frost At Dawn has the course-and-distance form and wears first-time cheekpieces that may spark a revival, though a disappointing 2025 campaign so far leaves plenty to prove from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's five-year-old mare has been placed twice at 5f on similar going and Barry McHugh rides; the sim-going record is thin (2/15) and her natural prominent inclination will be frustrated by the number of faster-away rivals in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 2¼ lengths when second at York latest, Heavenly Heather has been progressive, but ranked last of 26 on our figures and drawn in stall 22, this looks a big ask at the weights.

runners_data.name: Mgheera
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's six-year-old has placed at 5f before but the sim-going record of 5/15 is among the weakest in the field; Kieran Shoemark takes the ride and the horse has not finished better than fifth in recent starts, suggesting even a decent position early may not be enough.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and ranked well down our figures in a competitive field, Mgheera does at least have course-and-distance form on today's going and shaped with credit when beaten two lengths in a Group 2 last time, hinting at residual class.

runners_data.name: Miss Attitude
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's hold-up mare for Ronan Whelan, wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces; won at 5f on Good and her running style is genuine, but a 45-day absence and recent form of 10-745 tempers expectations in a race that looks likely to be won by a prominent racer.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 3 last time after missing the break, Miss Attitude's recent form reads consistently enough but she needs more to be competitive at this level, and ranked near the foot of our assessments, first-time cheekpieces must do the heavy lifting from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Monteille
runners_data.note: Mario Baratti's Italian-trained five-year-old with Cristian Demuro in the saddle; 80 days since his last run, zero wins on Good going in 15 attempts (sim-going 3/15), and his hold-up style is unlikely to be rewarded in a race where the pace should be controlled rather than collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent Group winner in France who ran creditably when beaten two lengths in a Group 1 last time out, but fast ground remains a concern and the 80-day absence gives pause — capable of mixing it, though conditions may again blunt the edge.

runners_data.name: Rayevka
runners_data.note: Graffard's four-year-old filly won at 5f on Soft last time but her 5/12 sim-going record and one Good-going win from 12 attempts is a concern; she has prominent instincts and Barzalona will want to be involved, but the front of this field is already crowded.|
runners_data.comment: Rayevka arrives in form after a convincing Group 3 win at Longchamp 37 days ago, benefitting from a drop in trip and grade, and ran well at this very meeting last year — stiff 5f on today's going looks ideal, though 130lb and a field of 26 pose stiff tasks.

runners_data.name: Rosy Affair
runners_data.note: George Boughey's five-year-old mare has three wins at 6f on Soft and Good, and Billy Loughnane rides; the note here is that she is a genuine pace runner mapped to hold-up because the prominent positions are oversubscribed, making this her least favourable scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Rosy Affair arrives on the back of a Listed win at Haydock 25 days ago and has won three of her last five starts, but stepping up in class looks the key question for this progressive mare, who handles today's trip and conditions well enough.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old won at 6f on Good and has a 7/10 sim-going record; Richard Kingscote partners and the horse races prominently, though a 5f trip at Group 1 level with a 34-day gap and best form at 6f remains a distance query.|
runners_data.comment: Landed the Commonwealth Cup at this very meeting 12 months ago, so course form reads perfectly, and a trainer firing on all cylinders adds to the appeal after a first-run reappearance at York that arguably underflattered — there should be more to come. The wide draw from stall 9 is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Aspect Island
runners_data.note: James Owen's three-year-old has been placed three times at 5f on Good and Firm, Silvestre De Sousa rides with a visor, and the horse is among the younger runners in the field; a natural prominent racer, he joins the long list of pace types for whom the positional arithmetic will not add up in a 26-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sprinter who ran a game race when a close third in Listed company last time out, but has been placed at the highest level and this demands even more again; the first-time visor is an interesting move, though, and 117 on our ratings suggests there's ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: Behike
runners_data.note: George Scott's exciting three-year-old with two wins from three starts, latterly at 6f on Good and Standard; David Egan rides and the horse is lightly raced enough that his ceiling is genuinely unknown, though the drop to 5f on Good to Firm against seasoned sprinters is a significant step up in class and distance challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Boasts back-to-back wins including a cosy novice success at Lingfield last time, but steps up sharply in grade now and, ranked 20th of 26 in the field, this looks a big ask so early in its career.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old has five wins from eight starts with a remarkable 6/8 sim-going record, Ryan Moore takes the ride, and back-to-back wins at 5f on Good most recently make this one of the most relevant profile horses in the race; the key question is whether Moore can position him close enough to the pace to deploy that turn of foot.|
runners_data.comment: Confirmed the improvement shown as a two-year-old by winning a Listed sprint at Naas last time out, and still progressing with a top course jockey aboard; the step back to five furlongs from stall 24 on 127 lb may test, as connections likely prefer six.

races.paceDynamic: Big Mojo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 26-horse sprint field on Good to Firm at Ascot, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Tom Marquand can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a significant positional advantage in a race this large. Behind him, Night Raider, American Affair, Cover Up, Rumstar, Overpass, Asfoora, Mission Central, Starlust, and Time For Sandals are the prominent types most likely to secure their natural racing position in the first third of the field, while runners like Rayevka, Jakajaro, Jm Jungle, Shagraan, Frost At Dawn, Getreadytorumble, and others are genuine front-runners or prominent racers who will find themselves shuffled back mid-pack simply because the positions do not exist for all of them. With Big Mojo able to bowl along at a comfortable clip without pressure, the pace will be honest but not brutal, meaning the leader and those stalking close to him in the first few lengths are best placed to sustain their momentum. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in the first three to six lengths — especially those who can be slotted in close to the pace by an experienced jockey — because the uncontested lead removes the energy-sapping early scrimmage that would ordinarily bring closers into play.

races.name: St James's Palace Stakes (Group 1) (Colts)

runners_data.name: Bow Echo
runners_data.note: Four wins from four starts all at a mile on Good ground, and Billy Loughnane partners a horse that has led throughout every time; with 45 days between runs the freshness angle is real, though STYLE_FIT tag is minor given he is actually the most natural pace-setter here and his unbeaten record makes him impossible to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Four wins on the spin culminate in a dominant 3-length 2000 Guineas success, where Bow Echo travelled supremely and quickened clear — a performance that marks him as the one to beat here, with proven course-and-distance form and 45 days to recover in good order.

runners_data.name: Gstaad
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien whose yard is firing at 7/31 over 14 days; seven from eight runs on similar going and three wins at the mile underline genuine class at the trip, and a prominent pitch suits his natural style, making him the horse most likely to secure a genuine Position 2 slot as the field settles.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time, quickening smartly to win by three lengths and advertise top-class mile form; proven on today's going and distance, with a top course jockey aboard from stall 1, though reversing Newmarket form remains the chief task.

runners_data.name: Lord Britain
runners_data.note: Won his last start over seven furlongs on Standard going but the Ascot mile on Good To Firm is a significant step up in class and on a surface he has struggled with historically (2 from 7 on similar going, no wins); he is a natural pace-seeker yet the congested pace map means he is likely to find himself racing further back than his style demands, which materially undermines his winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: Lord Britain won a handicap at Kempton last time on the all-weather, but is yet to prove effectiveness on turf and looks out of depth here; the first-time headgear may help, but this trip and surface combination remains unproven and our figures rank him last of six.

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: Returned a win over six furlongs before placed efforts at a mile — the trip looks workable — and David Egan rides a horse that wants to be prominent, but eight of nine runs have been on similar going without dominating, and with the pace map crowded he faces a battle to hold his preferred position against classier rivals.
runners_data.comment: Power Blue showed Group 1 credentials when fourth in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time but faces a re-opposing rival it couldn't beat there, and ranked fifth of six on our figures, a repeat performance looks unlikely to be enough here.

runners_data.name: Puerto Rico
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins at seven to eight furlongs including twice on Good ground for Soumillon and O'Brien, so the form and connections are serious, but the redistribution to a hold-up position is artificial — this horse's instinct is to race prominently and being forced to sit out the back in a six-runner field on a flat straight track is a tactical disadvantage he may not overcome.
runners_data.comment: Puerto Rico brings a fine recent profile with two G1 victories to its name and an upward curve through the backend of last season, and a closing fourth in the Poule d'Essai at Longchamp on its return suggests the spark remains — the key question is whether it can reproduce that form on quicker ground today.

runners_data.name: Talk Of New York
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick team up with a horse who has won three of his last four including a Listed success at the mile on Good; genuine prominent racer with strong recent form, and Buick's positional intelligence at Ascot's straight mile gives him every chance of securing a forward berth even in this pace-congested heat — headgear (h) noted.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in its last four starts, including a scintillating 5½-length Listed victory at Sandown last time out, mark Talk Of New York as a serious threat; a trainer in form and a step up to today's mile suiting ideally, though first-time headgear adds a small unknown at this higher level.

races.paceDynamic: Bow Echo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field where every other runner — Gstaad, Lord Britain, Power Blue, Puerto Rico, and Talk Of New York — is a natural prominent racer, meaning this race carries significant pace pressure despite the small field. Bow Echo will attempt to lead from the gates on Good To Firm ground at Ascot's straight mile, but with five horses all wanting to race prominently behind him, the early fractions are likely to be honest rather than dawdling, giving Bow Echo little opportunity to control tempo at his own leisure. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Gstaad, with Ryan Moore in the saddle and the strongest profile at the trip, is best-placed to actually hold a genuine prominent berth, while Talk Of New York (Buick/Appleby) and Power Blue are the next most likely to press for position, leaving Lord Britain and Puerto Rico pushed wider and further back than ideal. This race shape — a sustainably-run pace on fast ground with a compressed, pace-heavy field — favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a decisive turn of foot in the final two furlongs, giving a clear edge to genuine prominent-to-midfield gallopers who are comfortable on quick going.

watchPoints.text: Gstaad's position at the start is critical — if Ryan Moore gets him slotted immediately behind Bow Echo in second, he controls the race from a position of maximum comfort and becomes very hard to pass on the run to the line.

The cluster of natural prominent types — Talk Of New York, Power Blue, and Lord Britain — scrapping for positions two through four in the first furlong could cause early bumping or a faster-than-intended pace, which would change the complexion of this race entirely for Bow Echo.

Puerto Rico's actual running style is prominent, not hold-up; if Soumillon elects to push forward and reclaim his horse's natural position early, the pace shape becomes genuinely pressured and Bow Echo faces a credible challenger for the lead.

Good To Firm confirmed for the 4:20 race — the fast surface at Ascot's straight mile historically benefits horses that travel prominently and have a quick, decisive change of gear rather than those who need time to wind up from off the pace.

Lord Britain's OR of 88 represents a significant class drop relative to Bow Echo (126) and Gstaad (120); in a Group 1 with this much pace, he is the runner most vulnerable to being physically outpaced early even before the redistribution factor is considered.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here; Ian Williams confirms he goes forward, 11 days fresh, but on Good to Firm he has a credible recent profile (sim-going 6/15, 2W3P) and sets the race's entire tempo — his chance of winning depends on whether this becomes a true test or a dawdle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but shaped with plenty of promise before flopping over a sharp trip last time; back up in distance today suits ideally, acts on this going, and first-time headgear could sharpen focus — though the trainer's current form gives pause.

runners_data.name: Bunting
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up stayer for Mullins returning after 248 days off, Harry Vigors (7) riding; Ascot 2m4f on good ground suits his profile (6th in this race previously) and the late-run shape this race is likely to produce plays right into his hands.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last four starts and found little when comfortably held last time, Bunting's best form has come over staying trips on the Flat, though it looks stable second string here and inconsistency over hurdles remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Barnso
runners_data.note: Alan King runner back from 248 days off, Rossa Ryan up; wants to race prominently but ran 18th here on Good last time, and the long absence combined with a crowded prominent berth is a concern — may find himself shuffled back against his wishes.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts with a string of fourths before a below-par latest effort, Barnso is winless in its last five but the step up to 14f-plus looks key — stamina questions loom on reappearance after 248 days off, however.

runners_data.name: Reaching High
runners_data.note: Long absence (364 days) for Mullins with Ryan Moore; showed form at 2m on good and has a win at 14f on good, but has only run twice in this going band with no wins — the trip extension to 2m4f is the key unknown after this layoff.
runners_data.comment: Unlucky not to have won this 12 months ago when never getting a clear run and eased down beaten four lengths off the same mark, Reaching High lines up off an unchanged rating with course form and a top jockey aboard — the layoff is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for James Owen, Cieren Fallon aboard; visor retained, ran 1st over 21f on Soft and 3rd here over 16f on Good — the step up to 2m4f suits this profile and good ground is no barrier based on recent evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and below par in recent outings, Lavender Hill Mob faces a stiff mark at 94, though the first-time visor and effectiveness across any going are mild positives worth monitoring after a 60-day break.

runners_data.name: Mordor
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends over a horse who has won over 14f on Headford and placed at 24f on Good — genuinely versatile stayer; Jamie Spencer will want a prominent pitch and his recent win (1020-1 form) makes him the most credible of the front-tracking brigade.
runners_data.comment: Scored off a 7lb lower mark three starts back but was outstayed stepped up in trip last time; drops a significant 30lb here on a sound surface that suits, and proven course-and-distance form gives it every chance despite the inconsistent recent profile.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for J P O'Brien, Colin Keane riding; has placed in three of last five and won over 16f, largely on Heather/AW — good ground record is thinner than rivals and 2m4f is a step into new territory, but the trainer's powerful week warrants respect.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a close fourth at Chester last time off a 1lb lower mark, and this unexposed stayer's fine recent profile — including a runner-up effort — plus a significant jockey booking make her a leading danger, though she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: Racing out of a prominent role but blinkered, returning from 44 days with a P (pulled up) last time out and a string of below-par efforts — the headgear and O'Brien's stable being in form are positives, but the recent form line is deeply concerning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulled up at Cork latest when the ground proved too testing, Comfort Zone is only 1lb higher than when placing in this race last year, giving it a clear angle — though below-par form this term is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Siempre Arturo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type at heart wearing a hood; all five recent runs are over trips well short of 2m4f (maximum 12f in the past) and on mostly Standard/All-Weather — the trip and course combination looks a significant step into the unknown.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces and a 38-day break since a run that needed, Siempre Arturo has the versatility across trips and surfaces to be competitive, but patchy recent form and the step up in trip still required leave this one looking a place player at best.

runners_data.name: Defiantly
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides for O'Brien on a four-year-old who wears blinkers; placed at 14f on Good twice, won at 12f on Soft — the distance is the question mark but the going suits and the stable is firing; a hold-up profile that would benefit from the anticipated late-run shape.
runners_data.comment: Blinkers go on for the first time and there's a distance uptick that could suit this lightly-raced stayer, but inconsistent recent form and a lowly ranking on our figures make it hard to fancy with confidence.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin partners a four-year-old in excellent recent form (11-651), with a win over 16f on Good just 25 days ago — genuinely prominent-racing type who fits the second-row berth if he can get it; the Ascot straight should suit his sustained gallop.
runners_data.comment: Bahadur lands in the crosshairs here after a willing 1¼-length Goodwood handicap success last time out, and this hugely progressive stayer looks the type with more to give over this trip — the main risk being a 4lb higher mark than when scoring.

runners_data.name: Tim Toe

runners_data.name: Kizlyar
runners_data.note: O'Brien's four-year-old with J M Sheridan up, won over 14f on Good 35 days ago; has a tongue-tie and a genuine front-tracking tendency that has been redistributed to midfield here — trip extension to 2m4f is unproven, and racing out of role compounds the concern, though the current trainer form is not to be ignored.
runners_data.comment: Kizlyar bounced back to win at Killarney last time out but sits at the foot of our rankings and looks to need plenty here; the ex-French gelding is lightly raced over marathon trips and a potentially lenient mark offers the sole grounds for optimism, with first-time headgear adding a wildcard.

races.paceDynamic: Beylerbeyi is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 20-horse field and, with Billy Loughnane aboard, is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m4f on Good to Firm ground — there is no rival likely to pressurise him seriously from the front. Behind him, the prominent berths are bitterly contested: Mordor, Barnso, Galileo Dame, Comfort Zone, Bahadur, and Ismahane all want to race in the first half-dozen, yet only three or four can physically occupy those spots, meaning several will be shuffled into unfamiliar midfield slots. The hold-up brigade — Bunting, Lavender Hill Mob, Defiantly, Siempre Arturo, Westminster Moon, and Glenroyal — will be racing from further back than usual as the field compresses in behind a single genuine pacemaker. With one honest but uncontested lead and a moderate, even tempo anticipated over a stamina-sapping 2m4f, this race shape firmly favours hold-up horses and stayers who can travel sweetly through a compressed mid-race, then deploy a sustained late run from the widest, cleanest ground in the straight — positional jostling early will sap the energy of those forced to race out of role.

watchPoints.text: Beylerbeyi sets the only confirmed lead in a 20-runner field — if Billy Loughnane elects to increase tempo on the final turn to stretch the field, horses mapped from midfield outward will face an impossible task, so watch for any early signs of Beylerbeyi extending on the back straight.

Mordor and Bahadur are the two most credible horses actually capable of tracking Beylerbeyi at the head of the field — if either gets into a prime second-row position uncontested before the home turn, their stamina profiles make them live dangers in the straight.

The prominent berths are dangerously overcrowded: Kizlyar, Small Fry, Tim Toe, Puturhandstogether and All In You are all natural front-trackers; watch the first two furlongs for scrimmaging as these horses seek position, since any that expend energy fighting for ground early will pay in the final half-mile.

Westminster Moon makes a massive leap from 14f to 2m4f off just 23 days — if Seamie Heffernan can nurse him through the first mile, the good ground suits, but watch whether he drops his head and settles rather than over-racing on the wide Ascot track.

Lavender Hill Mob and Bunting are the two truest hold-up stayers in the field; both thrive on a strong gallop that tests stamina, and in a race with a single, sustainable pacemaker the question is whether the tempo is brisk enough to suit them — watch how Cieren Fallon and Harry Vigors (7) choose to position them in the first half-mile as an indicator of whether they think the pace is honest.

races.name: Wolferton Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Adelaide River
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose best form comes at 10f on good ground for O'Brien; a natural race-leader by instinct, he will find himself shuffled into midfield in this traffic-heavy field, which blunts his primary weapon and makes a big run unlikely.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Adelaide River faces a stiff ask here, though first-time headgear and a return to his best trip could help — he's back in Ireland needing to prove he retains the level that once made him a Group winner.

runners_data.name: Ancient Wisdom
runners_data.note: Appleby's five-year-old has been off 181 days but shaped well at Listed level in soft ground last autumn; switches here to Good to Firm which is untested in his recent profile, though his 10-12f Goodwood and York form suggests he handles quick ground — likely to occupy a genuine second-row position.|
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces applied for the first time and a trainer in cracking form give Ancient Wisdom every chance on this surface, with proven course-and-distance form working in its favour — though the going remains the key concern for this winless-in-recent-starts performer, who was below-par on her latest All-Weather outing.

runners_data.name: Arabian Light
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on good ground at Sandown last time; Buick takes the ride for Appleby but this horse naturally wants to be prominent and with so many rivals seeking the same ground, he faces a test of adaptability if shuffled back mid-race.|
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when fourth at Sandown 19 days ago on a sound surface, and today's trip and conditions suit; a consistent Group 3 performer with a trainer in form, though ranked 10th of 16 here and likely needs improvement to land the spoils.

runners_data.name: Dividend
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a sharp recent form string including back-to-back wins; trained by Newland and Insole, he is a natural front-pace horse who will find the prominent berths taken, and his optimum 9f trip makes the 1m2f a stamina query on top of the positional compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten just four lengths in a Group 1 in Dubai last time out gives Dividend some credibility, and it acts on today's going, but an 80-day break, first-time headgear, and a ranking of 15th of 16 on our figures make it very hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Enfjaar
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's six-year-old has posted consistent placed efforts at 10f on good ground throughout his career but has not won in five starts; naturally up-with-the-pace, he will be squeezed into the middle of this big field and his 0W4P similar-going record raises questions.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer whose good Goodwood Listed third on reappearance leaves him with improvement to come, and the yard has a strong record in this race — though winless in his last four starts remains the one reservation.

runners_data.name: Galen
runners_data.note: O'Brien's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose best efforts come from off the pace; posted a brilliant 2nd at 10f on good ground, and Dylan Browne McMonagle gives him every chance of organising a big finish — his 14/15 similar-going stat is the best in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts yet a Group winner with a solid second in this race last year, Galen has clear course-and-distance credentials on a sound surface; however, the 122-day break and a thumping in Grade/Group company last time raise questions, even if first-time headgear could sharpen matters.

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins raider who has won at the highest level over 10-12f on standard and good ground; natural front-pace style will be compromised in this big field but his class at the trip is real — Colin Keane needs to find a smooth passage from midfield.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Gaucher faces a stiff task off 131 lb from stall 12, and 74 days off gives pause — though first-time headgear, a top jockey back aboard, and two wins in its last four starts for a powerful Irish yard offer crumbs of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ghostwriter
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner: 360 days off the track but has done it fresh before; if he comes here in top shape he controls the fractions entirely and at OR 116 he is the highest-rated runner — the layoff is the only doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of credit when a close third in a Group 2 last time out, and this represents a markedly easier task for a proven top-level performer who acts on today's ground and distance — the sole concern is whether 360 days off the track leaves him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Haatem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old won at 10f on good ground at Goodwood last summer and has been placed at this level; James Doyle rides and he is one of the few horses likely to get a genuine prominent berth without fighting for it, sitting second or third on the bridle.|
runners_data.comment: Won this race last year and shaped with promise on his comeback at Goodwood 25 days ago, beaten three lengths in Listed company — that run under his belt should sharpen him up, though his last two efforts before that give reason for caution.

runners_data.name: King's Gambit
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's five-year-old finished 2nd twice at 9f on good ground; naturally wants a prominent pitch but will be outgunned for that position here, and his best trip looks a furlong or two shorter than today's 1m2f.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and below form when beaten eight lengths last time, King's Gambit nonetheless has placed twice in recent runs and acts on any going over today's trip — though connections may need to deploy him earlier than last year to turn placed efforts into something more.

runners_data.name: Map Of Stars
runners_data.note: French-trained by Graffard, handled by James McDonald; best form is at 10-12f on soft or heavy — his 3/12 similar-going record is the weakest in the field and Good to Firm Ascot looks a significant ask.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and comfortably held in a Group 3 last time, Map Of Stars looks a stiff ask from stall 10 carrying 131 lb, ranked bottom of these on our figures. First-time cheekpieces and a useful run at this meeting last year offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Nahraan
runners_data.note: Gosden's four-year-old arrived with a three-timer under his belt including a Listed win at 11f on good; 275 days off the track and only 2/4 on similar going — Oisin Murphy picks him up but the comeback plus the long absence makes this a speculative profile.|
runners_data.comment: Nahraan showed smart form when winning three of his last four starts, but returns from a 275-day absence to tackle what looks a stiff ask, and despite a trainer firing at 29%, this comeback run may come too soon for a colt still with plenty of improvement ahead.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type, last seen 11 days ago when finishing 2nd at 8f; dropping into the midfield-to-rear group naturally, Sean Levey will be hunting a late run but her best form is short of today's trip.|

runners_data.name: Royal Rhyme
runners_data.note: K R Burke's six-year-old has placed at this level at 10f on good and soft ground but has never won at Listed level in five attempts; figures to land in a genuine prominent spot without redistribution pressure, though his 0W0P record on similar going is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Royal Rhyme shaped with plenty of encouragement when finishing well after being caught too far back in a Group 2 last time, and a former Group winner returning to form with strong course claims, today's first-time headgear could be the spark that sees this winless-of-late performer finally deliver.

runners_data.name: Wimbledon Hawkeye
runners_data.note: James Owen's four-year-old won at 10f on firm ground and has placed twice over 12f on good; Cieren Fallon rides and he has a solid case on going and trip — headgear noted, and his 0W6P record suggests a consistent but hard-to-win profile.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths on return at Sandown last time but shaped as though that run will have sharpened him up, and he's a likeable Group 2/3 performer effective over this trip on any going; the first-time cheekpieces add an interesting angle, though 131 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Survie
runners_data.note: George Boughey's five-year-old won at 10f on standard ground and is a natural front-pace operator; Ryan Moore takes the ride and carries a 5lb allowance at 126lbs, but his instinct to bowl along early will be frustrated in this field and he has recorded just 0W4P on similar going.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Group 2 on her latest start 44 days ago, Survie has course-and-distance form and a top jockey aboard, while first-time headgear could sharpen her up — though she ideally wants cut in the ground, which is the key concern on today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Ghostwriter is the confirmed front-runner and, with a field of 16 mostly prominent-minded horses, will almost certainly slot into an uncontested lead at a sensible, controlled gallop — this is not a race where anyone is likely to press him aggressively in the early stages. The pace will be genuine but unhurried, set by Ghostwriter through the wide Ascot turns, with Ancient Wisdom, Haatem, Map Of Stars, Wimbledon Hawkeye and Royal Rhyme likely to occupy the realistic prominent positions behind him. This field carries far more front-running and prominent-type horses than the race shape can accommodate: Survie, Dividend, Arabian Light, Enfjaar, Nahraan, King's Gambit, Gaucher and Adelaide River are all natural up-with-the-pace horses who will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts, creating a condensed pack through the middle stages. The sustainable, single-pace gallop set by Ghostwriter on Good to Firm ground at Ascot — a track that consistently rewards horses travelling smoothly just behind the leader into the straight — decisively favours genuinely prominent types who can sit second or third on the bridle and kick for home turning in, rather than hold-up horses or those forced wide from a compromised position.

races.name: Copper Horse Stakes (Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who won over 20f last time, stepping back to 1m6f; strong record on good ground (2 wins, 5 places from 8 similar-going runs) and W J Lee makes the trip from Ireland, suggesting connections are serious — comfortable sitting prominently just off the pace is his natural mode.
runners_data.comment: Won off a 5lb lower mark on this card last year and effective over marathon trips on any ground, but Ascending may have reached a plateau and was well beaten in a Group 3 latest, suggesting the current mark is against it.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) notes this is out of his usual role; David O'Meara's horse has solid good-ground form but his OR-100 mark makes him a tough ask to beat from the front in a 16-runner field — uncontested lead is his only viable path.
runners_data.comment: Consistent prior to a puzzling below-par York flop latest, Stressfree ticks the boxes on distance and going and rates a leading danger on our figures — the main risk is whether that York run left its mark.

runners_data.name: Paddy The Squire
runners_data.note: Won twice at 12f on good ground before finishing sixth here at Royal Ascot on his last start; headgear (tongue-tie/pad) suggests stamina is managed carefully, and at 1m6f the step up in trip needs proving — Andrew Mullen keeps the ride for Iain Jardine.
runners_data.comment: Runners-up twice and a dual winner in recent starts, Paddy The Squire has course-distance-going form to draw on, but two disappointing efforts since those wins — including being outpaced and beaten over eight lengths at York — suggest the current mark may have caught up with him, and first-time cheekpieces plus a cold trainer compound the concern.

runners_data.name: Daiquiri Bay
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old who bounced back to winning form over 12f last time; Alan King has a modest 3/12 14-day strike rate but the horse's recent good-ground form (7/9 similar-going runs in frame) is compelling at this trip step-up.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who won a Boodles Handicap at Newmarket last time off a 4lb lower mark, but now racing off a revised rating that raises the bar; acts on today's conditions and distance, though the higher weight and mark are legitimate questions.

runners_data.name: Hallelujah U
runners_data.note: Has been off 318 days (213 days since a run for this jockey), a significant layoff flag; one win from 12f on good ground is his best reference, and returning from such a lengthy absence in a 16-runner handicap makes him hard to trust despite Luke Morris aboard with cheekpieces fitted.
runners_data.comment: Proven over course and distance, the first-time cheekpieces could sharpen this strong-staying type who acts on today's conditions, and the yard has a good record with similar profiles — though a disappointing latest run and an absence since leaves fitness the main query.

runners_data.name: Real Dream
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but recent form reads -64077, with no wins or places from 15 good-ground runs — Ian Williams has a 0/42 14-day strike and the t headgear hasn't sparked a revival; Barzalona takes over but the form figures demand caution.
runners_data.comment: Real Dream has been winless in its last five starts but arrives with the handicapper relenting and today's longer trip a clear plus on a sound surface it handles well; first-time headgear adds interest and our top rating of 119 marks this as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Yashin
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with headgear (hood/tongue-tie/blindfold) who finished 12th on his last good-ground run over 14f; Tom Marquand partners for Michael Bell but a 44-day break and uninspiring recent form (7606-0) make this a tough sell despite two career wins at similar going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and well beaten in a Newmarket handicap on his most recent outing 44 days ago, Yashin looks flattered by last year's Group win on this course and has been too inconsistent to fancy under a big weight, despite a significant jockey booking and proven course-and-distance form.

runners_data.name: Gamrai
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old is progressive and versatile in style, winning twice in his last five and recording a recent second over 12f on good ground; Oisin Murphy is a strong booking and the horse's 1W3P record from 6 similar-going starts hints at solid each-way claims if the trip comes good.
runners_data.comment: Quickened well but probably hit the front too soon and was caught late when second off a mark of 97 last time — 2lb higher here and ranked well down our figures, Gamrai looks up against it despite the yard winning this race last year.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who has won twice over 16f at Standard (all-weather) but records 0W0P from 15 good-ground starts — the going profile is a genuine concern for Cieren Fallon and the Ian Williams team who also saddle Real Dream; hard to strongly recommend on turf figures alone.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 7¼ lengths at Carlisle last time when unsuited by the drop in trip, Enemy is better judged on earlier successes and remains on a competitive mark over today's distance and going — though a struggling trainer strike-rate and first-time headgear introduce some uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Valiancy
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old is a genuine prominent racer — five good-ground starts, three wins including back-to-back 14f victories — but redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with front-end types; James Doyle will likely push forward, and if he secures a prominent position, the form profile makes him a leading player.
runners_data.comment: Boasts a fine recent sequence — three wins in its last five starts, including a cosy 1¼-length handicap success at Hamilton off a mark 8lb lower than today — and is a rapidly progressing stayer with more improvement expected; the 8lb rise and 136lb burden are the chief concerns for a trainer firing at 37%.

runners_data.name: Green Cape
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's runner has been off 129 days and returns with a tongue-tie; a natural front-end racer pushed back on the map by field congestion, but his recent form (514-94) and limited good-ground record (0W from 9 similar-going runs) make him a harder proposition to back on a comeback start.
runners_data.comment: Green Cape is last on our figures and has been inconsistent in recent starts, while 129 days off the track adds to the query marks; first-time cheekpieces and a switch of stable offer slim hope, but this looks a tough ask at the weights.

runners_data.name: Aeronautic
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old arrives after 116 days off with a tongue-tie, and although he is a genuine prominent-style horse by instinct, the map congestion means he may find himself further back than ideal; his best form (3 places at 13-14f) is respectable but one win from 11 similar-going runs limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and comfortably held in a Group 3 last time out, Aeronautic holds few secrets from the handicapper and returns after a 116-day break; first-time headgear and proven course-and-distance form offer slim positives, but this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Duraji
runners_data.note: Legitimate hold-up performer who won over 18f on good ground earlier in the season — the trip today at 1m6f might be on the sharp side; Finley Marsh is a 3lb claimer, and while the 39-day break is not concerning, a string of moderate finishes since that win needs explaining.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who shaped with promise at Chester last time, beaten a length off a 2lb lower mark, and a drop in trip looks a plus; winless in recent starts and a hefty 135lb may test its chances of converting.

runners_data.name: Sing Us A Song
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old won over 14f on soft last time and returned a solid second over 12f on good ground; James McDonald is a high-profile booking and, as a true front-end racer redistributed to midfield here, McDonald may seek to push forward early — if he gets his position, a big run is possible.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a game second at York last time off a 2lb lower mark, and there's reason to think longer distances will unlock more — effective at 12-14f and potentially better beyond, though today's trip and the 135lb burden are the key variables to weigh.

runners_data.name: Ernst Blofeld
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Standard last time and is lightly raced on turf; off only 20 days and Billy Loughnane takes over from the Hamad Al Jehani yard which has a low 3/7 14-day record — his one good-ground placing came at 12f and 1m6f is an unknown, making him a speculative hold-up each-way play at best.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Kempton handicap off a 7lb lower mark last time, so the revised rating makes this considerably tougher, and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, it's hard to fancy despite proven ability on today's going over this trip.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's five-year-old has placed twice at 12f on good ground and is a natural prominent-style horse bumped back on the map by field congestion; the trainer has a 0/7 14-day record and the horse's best form suggests the step to 1m6f could be stretching — Kieran Shoemark will need to find an ideal spot to compensate for the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Consistent filly who proved her Listed-class credentials with a close third at Goodwood 46 days ago, and she's proven effective over today's trip on this surface — the main worry is that she remains winless in her last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Stressfree is the only confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 1m6f handicap and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure — with all the other natural front-end types (Valiancy, Green Cape, Aeronautic, Sing Us A Song, Incensed) redistributed to midfield because the field is simply too deep in prominent-style horses for them all to race where they want. Stressfree will therefore bowl along at a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground, with Ascending, Paddy The Squire, Daiquiri Bay and Gamrai likely to sit just behind in a compact early group. The field contains more genuine prominent racers than the race shape can accommodate — Valiancy and Sing Us A Song are the most likely to push forward from their nominal midfield positions, and any early jostling for position could inject more pace than the headline map suggests. A measured, uncontested tempo over this staying trip on fast ground will suit horses that can travel prominently behind the pace or produce a powerful sustained gallop from midfield, rather than those relying on a late burst from off the pace — this race shape broadly favours hold-up types only if the gallop quickens materially in the straight, which is not guaranteed with a lone confirmed front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Valiancy (James Doyle) is a confirmed three-time good-ground winner who is mapped to midfield purely due to field congestion — watch whether Doyle pushes forward to his natural prominent position from the gate, because if he does, this is a serious winning chance.

Sing Us A Song (James McDonald) is another true front-end horse mapped to midfield; McDonald is one of the most assertive jockeys in the race and may force the issue early, which could materially lift the pace above what the Stressfree-only front-runner map implies.

Hallelujah U has not raced for 318 days and Stressfree carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 — two of the most prominently positioned horses on the map have significant form or fitness concerns, and if either underperforms early, the race shape could shift quickly towards hold-up runners.

Enemy and Real Dream (both Ian Williams, 0/42 14-day strike) are hold-up types whose good-ground records are poor (0W0P and 0W3P respectively at similar going) — if this pair run true to their turf form, the hold-up scenario loses two of its supposedly most qualified candidates.

Gamrai (Oisin Murphy, Gosden) has won or placed in 4 of 6 similar-going starts and steps up in trip for the first time to 1m6f — monitor early market moves to gauge whether connections are confident the distance is within his compass.
